==English==
{{wp}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|pănt}}
* {{IPA|en|/pænt/|a=RP,GenAm}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-pant.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/pant/|a=SSB,Northern England,Scotland,Wales}}
* {{IPA|en|/pæːnt/|[pʰẽːnt̚]|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/pɛnt/|a=NZ}}
* {{rhymes|en|ænt|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=breath|:inh|enm:panten|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|panten}}, whence also English dialectal {{m|en|pank}}.

Possibly from {{der|en|fro|pantoyer}}, a byform or of {{der|en|fro|pantoisier||to be breathless}} (compare modern {{cog|fr|panteler||to gasp for breath}}), of uncertain origin. Possibly from {{der|en|la-vul|*pantasiō||struggling for breath when having a nightmare}}, from {{der|en|grc|φαντασιόω||to be subject to hallucinations}}, from {{m|grc|φαντασία||appearance, image, fantasy}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# A quick [[breathe|breathing]]; a catching of the breath; a [[gasp]]: the panting of animals such as a dog with their tong hung out- as a form of thermoregulation.
# {{lb|en|figurative}} [[eager|Eager]] [[longing]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1995|author=John C. Leggett; Suzanne Malm|title=The Eighteen Stages of Love|page=9
|passage=Indeed, the projections, cravings, and everyday frolics common to trysts among buzz-activist Hollywood stars and starlets, plus their many common folk imitators, go forward with eager '''pant'''.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A violent [[palpitation]] of the [[heart]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Antony and Cleopatra|IV|viii|360|2|To this great fairy I'll commend thy acts, / Make her thanks bless thee. O thou day o' the world, / Chain mine arm'd neck; leap thou, attire and all; / Through proof of harness to my heart, and there / Ride on the '''pants''' triumphing.}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[breathe]] [[quickly]] or in a [[labored]] manner, as after [[exertion]] or from [[eagerness]] or [[excitement]]; to [[respire]] with heaving of the [[breast]]; to [[gasp#Verb|gasp]].
#* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis|passage=Pluto '''pants''' for breath from out his cell.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1820|author=w:Percy Bysshe Shelley|title=s:Prometheus Unbound
|passage=There is a cavern where my spirit / Was '''panted''' forth in anguish.}}
#* {{RQ:Cleland Fanny Hill|passage=Charles had just slipp'd the bolt of the door, and running, caught me in his arms, and lifting me from the ground, with his lips glew'd to mine, bore me, trembling, '''panting''', dying, with soft fears and tender wishes, to the bed}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To long [[eagerly]]; to [[desire]] [[earnestly]].
#* {{RQ:KJV|Psalms|42|1|passage=As the hart '''panteth''' after the water brooks.}}
#* {{RQ:Pope Horace|Who '''pants''' for glory finds but short repose.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[long]] for (something); to be [[eager]] for (something).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1633|author=w:George Herbert|title=Love
|passage=Then shall our hearts '''pant''' thee.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} Of the heart, to [[beat]] with [[unnatural]] [[violence]] or [[rapidity]]; to [[palpitate]].
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|1|7|passage=Yet might her piteous heart be seen to '''pant''' and quake}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[sigh]]; to [[flutter]]; to [[languish]].
#* {{RQ:Pope Pastorals|page=750|passage=[T]he whiſp'ring Breeze / '''Pants''' on the Leaves, and dies upon the Trees.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[heave]], as the breast.
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[bulge]] and [[shrink]] successively, of iron hulls, etc.
